newsitem.title: CHINA: China defence minister to visit U.S. in December.
newsitem.headline: China defence minister to visit U.S. in December.

text.p: Chinese defence minister Chi Haotian will visit the United States in early December in the latest in a series of high-level military contacts intended to bolster slowly-warming ties, diplomats said on Saturday.
Chi would have meetings with senior U.S. military officials during his visit, the Beijing-based diplomats said but gave no details of his expected schedule.

Sino-U.S. military contacts have grown in recent months as part of a general warming in cross-Pacific relations that have long been battered by disputes over Taiwan, human rights, copyright piracy and weapons proliferation.
Chi told visiting U.S. admiral Joseph Prueher in September he hoped the improvement in ties would continue, but that Taiwan would be the focal point of ties between Beijing and Washington.
Relations between the two plunged in March when China conducted missile tests off the coast of Taiwan during the run-up to the island's first direct presidential election.
Washington responded by sending two aircraft carrier battle groups to the area, a move that infuriated Beijing.
Both sides say a series of high-level visits have since helped improve ties.
U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher is scheduled to hold talks in Beijing next week with Chinese President Jiang Zemin, Foreign Minister Qian Qichen and other leaders.
